for_you.text: Kill review done (single read): the 8 scored old books all lost money on paper in the window, every day, under both fail models (old pricing, without V). Formally they are "not decidable" because some trades never closed, but none shows an edge, so we drop them and focus on EXP-012. The live probe is ready on the code side; its dry run ends around 11:36Z. If clean, I'll give Helm the hashes and ask you to fund 0.5 SOL. Biggest finding today: an early dry-run timing (2 samples, nothing sent) puts our entries at an estimated 7–8 slots after a migration. On the old test data that is about the last point where EXP-012's margin stayed above zero; past ~12 slots it did not. That is test data, not proof that EXP-012 makes money. I'm testing a faster feed: its first 3 events came 0.7–1.5 s earlier, at an estimated few thousand Helius credits a day.

Before the 10-16 result, I wrote down exactly what would have to hold for a pass to justify a small real-money trial. It must still win at the server's real speed and at your trial size, and the paper runner must agree with the scorer. I asked you for the trial size; the defaults are 0.5 SOL per trade, 3 at once. Nothing goes live without your yes.

I tried three ways to add more models to the forward test: a different sell rule, the same model retrained on more days, and a looser buy threshold for more trades. All three were checked on practice data under rules written down before looking, and none beat EXP-012 as it is (the extra trades from a looser threshold actually lose money). So EXP-012 stays the one forward test, which keeps its result clean. To genuinely use the data more, the next step is a different kind of signal, built on the new August data, for a later test window.

Better news on the free trade feed. In a calm 2-hour stretch this morning the fast server's tape caught every single trade on the chain (100%). The 15% it missed yesterday was lost while the connection kept dropping and reconnecting. So the free feed is good when stable; the fix is to make it survive reconnects (e.g. two connections at once, free), and to keep checking it against the chain record every hour.

Good early sign on the biggest risk for live trading. EXP-012's test assumed we buy in the very first moment after a token migrates. Our real feed is a few seconds behind, so I re-ran the strategy on its practice data with the buy delayed by up to 12 blocks (about 3 seconds). Profit per trade shrank by roughly 20% at a realistic 1–1.5 second delay, and by about 40% at 3 seconds, but it stayed positive throughout. This is practice data the model was built on, so it is a warning check, not proof. Separately, the backup test block (6 days) is fetched and verified, ready for the next test.

The free public trade feed misses trades. Checked against the chain record for 2 hours, the fast server's tape caught 84.759% of trades and the Oracle tape caught 66.241%, so the fast tape fails its 95% bar. In that window the 9 Oracle paper books saw only about two-thirds of the trades. The EXP-012 test data comes from full block downloads, so that result is unaffected. A second check in a calmer period is running now. If the free feed still falls short, the fix is to follow new blocks directly (about 9.7M Helius credits/month, inside budget).

EXP-012 passed its one-shot test on 6 never-seen days, under both fail models: 451 trades, about +0.035 SOL per trade (flat) and +0.021 (pressure), still positive without the top 3 trades. It is a replay, not money made, and the week was favourable (even unfiltered entries made money), with most of the edge coming from predicting which entries fill. Next is a forward-paper book on the fast server after the 10-05 kill review. Live needs that book to pass on its own trades, and then your approval.

EXP-012 is frozen and passed its pre-stated screen on the clean training data: 9 of 9 days positive under both fail models. On the fast-box data the test block comes from, the in-sample result is weaker (+4.19% flat, +3.25% pressure), so expect the read to be weaker still. The one-shot read of the fresh block happens today after the walkers finish (about 12:30Z plus verification). A pass there starts forward paper; it does not mean live yet.

Clean data is in. The exploration pool is deduplicated (2.47M duplicate trade rows removed, all in 3 resumed hours), and the entry-model idea still passes its screen on it. Next is EXP-012, a fresh one-shot test on a never-read 6-day block, which is fetching now on research-0. Expected read: today after about 12:00Z, if the re-frozen model passes its pre-stated check first.
EXP-011 closed NOT_DECIDABLE: the walkers wrote duplicate rows and one empty hour. No result was seen. Next: fix the data, re-check the entry model on clean data, then a new test on a fresh block.
